unmapped_findings: No numeric mechanical property values are reported specifically for Fe30Mn6Al1C (Al-6) after the 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment; only the qualitative engineering stress-strain (Fig. 2d) and work-hardening-rate (Fig. 8d) curves are available for this condition.

The tabulated tensile/impact properties (Table 2) and microstructural parameters (Table 3, e.g. Al-6: D_FCC-G/T = 34.2 ± 1.1 μm, f_Tw = 45.3%, no ferrite, κ-carbide size 0 nm, impact toughness 354 ± 16 J) are reported for the 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated condition, NOT for this 1100 °C/2 h sample, and are therefore not assigned to this sample.

After 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment the yield strength of the Al-containing steels shows a slight decrease relative to the 1050 °C/2 h condition, which is attributed to an increase in grain size with increasing solution-treatment temperature (b0027).

For the Al-series at 1100 °C the work-hardening-rate ordering is retained (6% Al highest, 12% Al lowest) and the true stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain (some beyond 0.5) than after 1050 °C (Fig. 8d).
The ultimate true stress (σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa) and fracture strength (σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa) remain nearly unchanged for the 1100 °C solution-treated samples as well (b0075).

Consistent with Fig. 5, no κ-carbides were observed in the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C low-density steel at low Al content (8% Al shown as representative); Al-6 (6% Al) is the lowest-Al member with the highest reported impact toughness in the alloy series.
